title: The Book of Matthew: Comprehension Quiz
description: Ten questions about the structure, teachings, and events in the Gospel of Matthew.

questions.prompt: Which four women, besides Mary, are named or referred to in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus?
options: Sarah, Rebekah, Rachel, and Leah
Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, and the wife of Uriah
Mary, Elizabeth, Anna, and the Queen of Sheba
Hagar, Dinah, Tamar, and Abigail
questions.explanation: Matthew 1 refers to Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, and the wife of Uriah (traditionally identified as Bathsheba). The text does not name the wife of Uriah here.

questions.prompt: How many major teaching discourses of Jesus are commonly identified in Matthew?
options: Three
Five
Seven
Twelve
questions.explanation: Matthew is commonly outlined around five major discourses, each followed by a concluding formula. The five-discourse structure is widely noted; claims that it deliberately mirrors the Torah are interpretive.

questions.prompt: In Matthew 5:17, what does Jesus say about His relationship to the Law and the Prophets?
options: He came to abolish them and establish a completely separate teaching
He came to suspend them until the resurrection
He came not to abolish them, but to fulfill them
He came to limit them to dietary and ritual observances
questions.explanation: Jesus says, “I have not come to abolish them but to fulfill them” (Matthew 5:17).

questions.prompt: Which two figures appear with Jesus at the Transfiguration in Matthew 17?
options: Abraham and David
David and Elijah
Moses and Elijah
Isaiah and Jeremiah
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:3 says that Moses and Elijah appeared and talked with Jesus.

questions.prompt: What does Simon Peter confess about Jesus in Matthew 16:16?
options: “You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God.”
“You are the suffering servant prophesied by Isaiah.”
“You are the king who has come to overthrow Rome.”
“You are a righteous teacher sent from God.”
questions.explanation: Peter answers, “You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God” (Matthew 16:16). Jesus then speaks of building His church on “this rock”; interpretations of that phrase vary among Christian traditions.

questions.prompt: What is the best description of Matthew's phrase “kingdom of heaven”?
options: It teaches a Gnostic separation of the spiritual realm from the physical world
It is Matthew's characteristic wording for God's reign and is generally used in a sense parallel to “kingdom of God”
It refers only to the afterlife, not to God's rule in the present
It distinguishes Roman citizenship from divine rule
questions.explanation: Matthew often uses “kingdom of heaven,” while other Gospel writers commonly use “kingdom of God.” The phrases are generally understood to refer to God's reign; explaining Matthew's wording specifically as reverential avoidance of the divine name is common, but not certain.

questions.prompt: In Jesus' explanation of the Parable of the Sower (Matthew 13:22), what does the seed sown among thorns represent?
options: People who hear the word but fall away when tribulation or persecution arises
People who hear the word, but worldly worries and the deceitfulness of wealth choke it
People who hear and understand the word, bearing a fruitful harvest
People who hear but do not understand, allowing the evil one to take the word away
questions.explanation: Jesus says that the worries of this age and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word, making it unfruitful.

questions.prompt: What happens to the temple curtain at the moment of Jesus' death in Matthew 27:51?
options: The golden lampstand stays lit for forty days
Fire consumes the altar of incense
The curtain of the temple is torn in two from top to bottom
The bronze sea overflows with water
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:51 reports that the temple curtain was torn in two from top to bottom; the passage also describes an earthquake and rocks splitting.

questions.prompt: Which recurring formula does Matthew use to connect events in Jesus' life with Scripture?
options: “As it is written in the book of the law of Moses...”
“This was to fulfill what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet...”
“Thus says the Lord Almighty to the house of Israel...”
“In accordance with the ancient covenant made with Abraham...”
questions.explanation: Matthew repeatedly uses variations of a fulfillment formula, such as “This was to fulfill what had been spoken by the Lord through the prophet.”

questions.prompt: How does the Gospel of Matthew conclude in chapter 28?
options: With Jesus' ascension from the Mount of Olives
With Paul arriving in Rome to preach to the Gentiles
With the Great Commission in Galilee and Jesus' promise to be with His disciples always
With the Day of Pentecost and the outpouring of the Holy Spirit
questions.explanation: Matthew ends with the risen Jesus commissioning His disciples on a mountain in Galilee and promising, “I am with you always, to the end of the age” (Matthew 28:20).
